Quick legal ops note and items to include in the buyer evidence pack. We can support the 9-month private offer but need to keep a few guardrails:

1) Marketplace constraints: AWS Marketplace tooling allows flexible offer durations but seller acceptance windows (the period the buyer has to sign) are typically 30 days. We can request a 45-day window but that is an ops escalation that will require Salesforce ticketing and an internal exception approval. Expect ~2 business days to request, and ops may still revert to 30 days. If Aurelia must have 45 days, we should surface that as an ask but continue with a 30-day default in the DocuSign envelope.

2) Contract/legal: for a sub-12 month term we need to ensure cancellation and refund language is clear. Don’t commit to refunds beyond prorated unused days. Jordan — please confirm the proration model (credit vs refund) and whether finance requires escrow for pilot.

3) Evidence pack (attach these):
- SOC2_Type2_2026.pdf (full report)
- DPA_summary.pdf (summary of data handling + regional controls)
- PenTest_Summary_2026.pdf (redacted)
- Network_Diagram_Public.pdf (high level)
- Aurelia_Signer_Roster.xlsx (template for buyer to fill)

4) Pricing/fees: Redwood can absorb the Marketplace transacting fee for this pilot to simplify procurement. Capture that as a one-time seller credit applied at activation.

5) Sanction/screening: procurement flagged sanctions screening for cross-border divisions — recommend we ask Aurelia to run a quick KYC/sanctions form and share the completed form before DocuSign. That will remove a common blocker and can be packaged with the evidence items.

I’ll prepare a short legal cover note to include in the DocuSign envelope outlining acceptance window, proration, and refund mechanics. Once Jordan confirms proration mechanics, Naomi can assemble and send.

—Vanessa Ortiz
